html.body: Date: 2025-04-04 REMARKSIntroduction Upon entry, claims 1-3, 5, 6, 8-10, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18-20 and 22 are pending in this application, of which claims 1 and 8 are independent. By this response, claims 1, 8, and 22 are amended, and claims 17 and 21 have been cancelled without prejudice. Claims 4, 7, 11, and 14 were previously cancelled. This Amendment does not generate new matter because the amendments to claims 1 and 8 incorporate subject matter from cancelled claims 17 and 21.The arguments and contentions presented herein should not be construed as any acquiescence or agreement by Applicant with the reasoning stated in the Office Action regardless of whether or not the following remarks specifically address any particular argument or contention from the Office Action. Furthermore, although certain distinctions between the claims of the present application and the cited references are addressed below, these distinctions are not necessarily exhaustive.Reconsideration of this application for allowance of all pending claims is hereby respectfully requested in view of the amendments to the claims and following remarks.Allowable Subject Matter Applicant acknowledges with appreciation that claims 17 and 21 are indicated as allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.Claim Reiections Under 35 U.S.C. § 103 Claims 1, 8, 15 and 19 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Park (U.S. Publication No. 2022/0332319, hereinafter "Park") in view of Shalev-Shwartz et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2021/0078570, hereinafter "Shalev-Shwartz").Claims 2, 3, 6, 9, 10 and 13 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Park in view of Shalev-Shwartz as applied to claims 1 and 8 above, and further in view of Grace et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2021/0304607, hereinafter "Grace").Claims 5 and 12 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Park in view of Shalev-Shwartz as applied to claims 1 and 8 above, and further in view of Kato (U.S. Publication No. 2020/0247417, hereinafter "Kato").Claims 16 and 20 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Park in view of Shalev as applied to claims 1 and 20 above, and further in view of Schmudderich et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2013/0054106, hereinafter "Schmudderich").Claims 18 and 22 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Park in view of Shalev as applied to claims 1 and 8 above, and further in view of Xue et al. (U.S.Publication No. 2022/0375349, hereinafter "Xue").Independent claim 1 is amended to include the features "the event prediction model is trained from a first point in time to a second point in time, ... the first point in time is a point in time at which the preceding vehicle starts to move from a same lane as a lane in which the autonomous driving vehicle is traveling to an adjacent lane, ... the second point in time is a point in time at which a portion of the preceding vehicle is located at a point in the adjacent lane, the point in the adjacent lane being separated by a predetermined distance from any one lane marking of the lane in which the preceding vehicle is traveling, and ... the preset event related to the preceding vehicle is predicted to occur at the second point in time," which Applicant believes is substantially similar to subject matter of claim 17 (which is indicated as allowable by the Examiner).Independent claim 8 is amended to include the features "the training of the event prediction model comprises training the event prediction model from a first point in time to a second point in time, ... the first point in time is a point in time at which the preceding vehicle starts to move from a same lane as a lane in which the autonomous driving vehicle is traveling to an adjacent lane, ... the second point in time is a point in time at which a portion of the preceding vehicle is located at a point in the adjacent lane, the point in the adjacent lane being separated by a predetermined distance from any one lane marking of the lane in which the preceding vehicle is traveling, and ... the preset event related to the preceding vehicle is predicted to occur at the second point in time," which Applicant believes is substantially similar to subject matter of claim 21 (which is indicated as allowable by the Examiner).In view of the foregoing amendments to claims 1 and 8, it is respectfully submitted that none of the cited art, whether taken alone or in combination, disclose, teach or suggest the aforementioned features of claims 1 and 8.Applicant therefore submits that claims 1 and 8 and the claims dependent thereupon are in condition for allowance, and the present application should pass to issue.Conclusion In view of the above amendments and remarks, Applicant submits that this application should be allowed and the case passed to issue. If there are any questions regarding this Amendment or the application in general, a telephone call to the undersigned would be appreciated to expedite the prosecution of the application.Applicant believes no fee is due with this response. However, if a fee is due, please charge our Deposit Account No. 50-0310 from which the undersigned is authorized to draw.Respectfully submitted, Dated: April 4, 2025 / Seungjae (Shawn) Lee / Seungjae (Shawn) Lee Registration No. 81,560 Customer No. 09629 MORGAN, LEWIS & BOCKIUS LLP1111 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW Washington, D.C. 20004 Phone: (202) 739-3000 Facsimile: (202) 739-3001
